Na mesma direção pesquisariam André Weil (1906-1998), autor de Fundamentos da Geometria Algébrica (1946), Friedrich Hirzebruch, nascido em 1927, autor de Novo Método Topológico em Geometria Algébrica (1956) e Claude Chevalley (1909-1984), autor, igualmente, de Fundamentos da Geometria Algébrica, de 1958. Wolfgang Krull (1899-1971), mais dedicado à Teoria dos anéis, sob influência de Emmy Noether, pesquisaria, igualmente, no campo da Geometria algébrica, com o emprego de Anéis no estudo de propriedades locais de variedades algébricas. That is an historical journey from Athens to São Carlos, going from the discovery of the Plato polyhedra to characteristic classes of a singular variety, by M.-H. Schwartz and R. MacPherson, from the Euler formula and Poincaré-Hopf Theorem to the study of local Euler obstruction. In 1965, Marie-Hélène Schwartz defined characteristic classes for singular complex varieties, as cohomology classes of an ambient manifold, with support on the singular varieties. In 1974, Robert MacPherson showed existence of homology characteristic classes for singular varieties, proving a Deligne and Grothendieck conjecture. One of the main ingredients of his definition is the local Euler obstruction, defined by differential forms. An equivalent definition of the local Euler obstruction, using vector fields, has been given by Jean-Paul Brasselet and MarieHélène Schwartz in their proof of the coincidence of two previous definitions of characteristic classes via Alexander isomorphism. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- HIGHER ALGEBRAIC K THEORY AN OVERVIEW LECTURE NOTES IN MATHEMATICS (https://prefeitura.aracaju.se.gov.br/fulldisplay/78hVIc/3AD111/HigherAlgebraicKTheoryAnOverviewLectureNotesInMathematics.pdf) 【turn704763726search2】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 11 months ago; Crawled: 7 months ago; #algebraic geometry #algebraic geometry k theory #algebraic k groups #algebraic k-theory #classifying spaces #coherent sheaves #exact categories #grothendieck group #higher algebraic k theory #higher k-theory #homotopy groups #homotopy theory #k theory lecture notes #motivic cohomology #number theory #q-construction #quillen k theory #quillen plus construction #topological quantum field theories #waldhausen categories These functors, denoted as K_n(R), capture important information about the ring R. The zeroth K-group, K_0(R), is essentially the Grothendieck group of finitely generated projective modules over R. The first K-group, K_1(R), is the abelianization of the general linear group GL(R). Higher K-groups, K_n(R) for n â‰¥ 2, are more intricate and require more sophisticated machinery to define. ### Higher Algebraic K-Theory: An Overview The study of higher algebraic K-theory involves understanding the structure and properties of these higher K-groups. One of the key tools in this area is the plus construction, which allows us to define higher K-groups in terms of homotopy groups of certain topological spaces associated with the ring. This approach was pioneered by Quillen in his seminal work on the subject. Another important aspect of higher algebraic K-theory is its connection to other areas of mathematics, such as algebraic topology, number theory, and algebraic geometry. For instance, the higher K-groups of a ring of integers in a number field are related to the class groups and unit groups of that field. Its connections to other areas of mathematics make it a vital area of study for anyone interested in the deeper structures of algebra and geometry. As our understanding of higher K-theory continues to grow, so too will our ability to apply its insights to a wide range of mathematical and scientific problems. ## Related Images Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 1 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 2 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 3 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 4 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 5 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 6 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 7 Image: higher algebraic k theory an overview lecture notes in mathematics image 8 ## Keyword Cluster #algebraic geometry #algebraic geometry k theory #algebraic k groups #algebraic k-theory #classifying spaces #coherent sheaves #exact categories #grothendieck group #higher algebraic k theory #higher k-theory #homotopy groups #homotopy theory #k theory lecture notes #motivic cohomology #number theory #q-construction #quillen k theory #quillen plus construction #topological quantum field theories #waldhausen categories -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ALGEBRAIC GEOMETRY ROBIN HARTSHORNE (https://prefeitura.aracaju.se.gov.br/browse/KWyBPZ/0AD019/AlgebraicGeometryRobinHartshorne.pdf) 【turn704763726search3】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 1.5 years ago; Crawled: 7 months ago; #algebraic geometry #algebraic geometry research #algebraic varieties #coherent sheaves #commutative algebra #cryptography #grothendieck schemes #hartshorne algebraic geometry textbook #intersection theory #mathematical physics algebraic geometry #quantum field theory #riemann-roch theorem #robin hartshorne #schemes #schemes in algebraic geometry #sheaf cohomology #string theory His work continues to inspire both students and researchers in understanding the complex relationships that algebraic geometry explores. ### Who Is Robin Hartshorne? Robin Hartshorne is a mathematician known primarily for his influential textbook "Algebraic Geometry," which has become a standard reference in graduate studies worldwide. Born in 1938, Hartshorne's contributions span many areas of algebraic geometry, but his pedagogical legacy is especially significant. His clear exposition helped demystify a subject that many consider abstract and difficult to grasp. ### The Essence of Algebraic Geometry Algebraic geometry studies the solutions to systems of polynomial equations, connecting algebraic methods with geometric intuition. It provides a framework for understanding shapes defined by polynomial constraints, known as algebraic varieties. This interplay between algebra and geometry has applications in number theory, complex analysis, and even physics. ### Hartshorneâ€™s Impact on Learning and Research The book covers a wide range of topics, from the basics of schemes and coherent sheaves to more advanced subjects like intersection theory and the Riemann-Roch theorem.
